questions.question: How can non-flash-based browser tools support AR rapid prototyping without requiring third-party browser plugins?
options: By sending all content and computation to a backend server
By writing code in HTML, WebGL, or similar web component technologies
By adding an AR plugin to an existing 3D authoring tool
By using an open-source C++ middleware framework
questions.explanation: Non-flash-based browser tools can avoid third-party browser plugins by letting developers use HTML, WebGL, or similar web component technologies to write their own fast prototype.

questions.question: Which description best matches Open Frameworks?
options: An open-source C++ middleware framework that provides tracking, rendering, and interaction support by combining libraries
A plugin that adds AR support to an existing interactive 3D authoring tool
A free AR browser application that runs on mobile devices as a prototyping tool
A standalone no-coding authoring tool that includes content authoring and AR support
questions.explanation: Open Frameworks is an open-source C++ middleware framework and library for desktop and mobile platforms, and for AR development it supports tracking, rendering, and interaction through combined libraries.

questions.question: Which statement describes Wikitude as a mobile prototyping tool?
options: It is an open-source C++ middleware framework for desktop and mobile platforms
It is a standalone authoring tool that requires no programming experience
It is a free AR browser application that runs on mobile devices
It is a plugin added to an existing interactive 3D authoring tool
questions.explanation: Wikitude is described as a free augmented reality browser application that runs on mobile devices as a useful mobile prototyping tool.

questions.question: How does Wikitude distribute work between the mobile device and servers?
options: The mobile device requires an open-source C++ framework to compute AR effects
The mobile device performs all computation and stores all content locally
The mobile device mainly acts as a client or renderer, while backend servers handle content and UI specifications
The mobile device uses a third-party browser plugin to obtain content from the web
questions.explanation: Wikitude treats the mobile device primarily as a client or rendering device, with the application connecting to backend servers for content and specification of user interface elements.

questions.question: What happens if developers do not have their own content when using Wikitude?
options: The tool automatically generates fully flexible custom content for them
They cannot use Wikitude for prototyping at all
They rely on default tool content, which may reduce flexibility but remains usable
The mobile device must run an open-source C++ middleware framework
questions.explanation: Wikitude makes prototyping easier or faster when developers have their own content; without content, developers depend on default content provided by the tool, which may reduce flexibility but is still usable.

questions.question: In an AR software plugin for an existing content authoring tool, what does the plugin mainly add?
options: A complete standalone authoring package that does not need another tool
A web prototype written directly in HTML and WebGL
Backend computation that lets the mobile device render only
AR-specific functions such as tracking, visualization, and 3D registration over the real-world view
questions.explanation: A plugin is added to an existing interactive 2D or 3D authoring tool and supplies AR-specific functions such as tracking, visualization, and 3D registration. The main authoring tool remains responsible for content authoring.

questions.question: Why can using an AR plugin be easy and quick for a developer?
options: The developer already knows the host authoring tool and only needs to understand the plugin
The developer avoids learning any part of the host tool or the plugin
The developer avoids dependence on proprietary player software
The approach remains sensible even if the developer has never used the authoring tool
questions.explanation: The plugin approach is easy and quick when the developer can rely on existing knowledge of the host authoring tool and only needs to learn the plugin. If the developer does not know the authoring tool, the approach makes no sense because everything must be learned from scratch.

questions.question: What is a limitation of adding AR support through a plugin to an existing authoring tool?
options: The user interface and interaction design can be limited to what the underlying authoring tool provides
The plugin can provide any interaction not already supported by the host tool
The content is usually independent of proprietary player software
The software and hardware configuration is independent of the underlying tool
questions.explanation: Plugins are constrained by the underlying authoring tool for user interface, interaction design, and software and hardware configuration. Content produced with the authoring tool usually also becomes dependent on proprietary player software in most cases.

questions.question: What approach can resolve the limitations of higher-level AR tools or plugins?
options: Use higher-level plugins and continue depending on a third-party tool
Use low-level software development tools, such as software libraries, and build the system from scratch
Use low-level software libraries while still leaving the system dependent on a third-party tool
Use a higher-level tool only to avoid building any part of the system from scratch
questions.explanation: A way to resolve the limitations of higher-level AR tools or plugins is to use low-level software development tools, such as software libraries, and build the system from scratch. This avoids depending on a third-party tool.

questions.question: What distinguishes standalone AR authoring tools from AR plugins?
options: They require a basic authoring tool to provide scene editing
They are low-level libraries that require building an AR system from scratch
They are complete packages that include content authoring and AR support without depending on another tool
They add AR functions to an existing content authoring tool
questions.explanation: Standalone AR authoring tools are complete packages that include both content authoring and AR support, unlike plugins that depend on an existing tool.

questions.question: Why can non-programmers use most standalone AR authoring tools?
options: They provide drag-and-drop graphical interfaces for creating experiences without coding
They require only command-line scripting languages
They demand knowledge of a host 3D authoring package
They rely on HTML and WebGL expertise to build prototypes
questions.explanation: Most standalone AR authoring tools use drag-and-drop GUIs so users with basic PC skills and no programming experience can create AR experiences.

questions.question: What range of features do standalone AR authoring tools typically support?
options: Scene construction, animation, and interactive behavior, from simple scenes to complex interactions
Only low-level rendering and device sensor access
Only static 2D image tracking and marker registration
Only audio mixing and haptic feedback
questions.explanation: Standalone AR authoring tools typically support scene construction, animation, and adding interactive behavior, with capabilities ranging from simple scene construction to complex interactive systems.

questions.question: What is a limitation of building an AR application with no coding in a standalone authoring tool?
options: It makes mobile deployment impossible
It prevents the use of drag-and-drop interfaces
It requires a host 3D authoring package
Its utility is limited compared with an advanced system that uses scripting for more flexibility
questions.explanation: Applications built with absolute zero coding have limited utility compared with advanced systems that use scripting-language support for more flexibility.

questions.question: How are augmented reality software categories ordered by the programming skill required?
options: Plugins to existing systems require the most skill, low-level libraries and frameworks require the least, and standalone authoring tools and rapid prototyping tools fall between these extremes.
Standalone authoring tools require the most skill, low-level libraries and frameworks require the least, and rapid prototyping tools and plugins fall between these extremes.
Low-level libraries and frameworks require the least skill, standalone authoring tools require the most, and rapid prototyping tools and plugins fall between these extremes.
Low-level libraries and frameworks require the most skill, standalone authoring tools require the least, and rapid prototyping tools and plugins fall between these extremes.
questions.explanation: AR software tools and packages fall into four categories based on programming skill: low-level libraries and frameworks require the highest skill, standalone authoring tools require the least, and rapid prototyping tools and plugins to existing systems lie between these extremes.

questions.question: When a developer adds an augmented reality plugin to an existing interactive three-dimensional graphics authoring tool, what makes the approach quick, and what aspects of the final augmented reality system can still be constrained by the host tool?
questions.reference_answer: A plugin is added to an existing content authoring tool and adds AR-specific functions such as tracking, visualization, and three-dimensional registration, while the host tool handles content authoring. It is quick when the developer already knows the host authoring tool because they only need to understand the plugin. However, user interface and interaction design, software and hardware configuration, and in most cases dependence of the content on proprietary player software are constrained by the underlying authoring tool.

questions.question: Why might a developer choose low-level software development tools instead of a higher-level augmented reality tool or plugin, and what does that choice demand of the developer?
questions.reference_answer: Low-level software development tools such as software libraries can resolve limitations of higher-level tools or plugins by letting the developer build the system from scratch rather than depending on a third-party tool. They demand the highest programming skill because low-level libraries and frameworks provide access to the core tracking and display functionality used to build an augmented reality application.

questions.question: How does Wikitude's client-server structure shape the role of the mobile device in augmented reality prototyping, and how does available content affect its usefulness?
questions.reference_answer: Wikitude is a free augmented reality browser application that runs on mobile devices and can be used as a mobile prototyping tool. It treats the mobile device primarily as a client or rendering device, connecting to backend servers for content and user interface elements, with computation possibly taking place on the backend server. It makes prototyping easier or faster when developers have their own content; without content, developers depend on default content, which may reduce flexibility but is still usable.

questions.question: How do standalone augmented reality authoring tools differ from plugins in what they provide to a developer, and what user skills are enough to begin using many of them?
questions.reference_answer: Standalone authoring tools allow users to create augmented reality experiences without programming experience and are complete packages that include content authoring and augmented reality support, unlike plugins, which require a basic content authoring tool on which augmented reality support is provided. They typically support scene construction, animation, and adding interactive behavior. Most provide drag-and-drop graphical user interfaces, so users with basic personal computer skills and non-programmers can learn and use them.
